acceptanceCriteria: Skip/close affordance reachable on all onboarding pages including the last
Next/Continue buttons >=44pt tall (migrated to .brandPrimary/.brandGhost)
Page indicator announces the current page to VoiceOver as it changes
ReduceMotion respected on page transitions

Declining persists the minimal-consent state and dismisses

Default toggle states reflect privacy-first defaults

acceptanceCriteria: Unlock button >=44pt tall (via .brandPrimary or .minHitTarget())
PremiumBadge reads as one combined element with a clear label (e.g. 'Insider feature, locked')
Lock icon marked decorative
No visual regression to the gate overlay

userStories.title: Hide decorative icons and combine star ratings for VoiceOver

acceptanceCriteria: Star rating rows announce a single 'N out of 5 stars' value

Award/sponsored badges carry meaningful labels (e.g. 'Best of Des Moines winner')
Applied consistently across event/restaurant/attraction cards and detail screens

Featured' when applicable); individual star Images, hero placeholder/type icons hidden. ContentCard placeholder image + AwardBadge trophy glyph marked .accessibilityHidden (the badge keeps its meaningful 'winner' label).

Snapshot/manual check at largest accessibility Dynamic Type shows no clipped titles
Visual hierarchy preserved

Left genuine non-ramp glyph/@ScaledMetric fonts untouched. No tokens absent from AppTypography introduced.

didRegisterForRemoteNotificationsWithDeviceToken fires on a real device and logs a token

Permission prompt appears at a deliberate moment (post-onboarding), not only on saved-search alert enable
checkPermissionStatus() consulted so a denied user is not re-prompted endlessly

userStories.title: Invoke DeepLinkHandler on URL and universal-link opens

acceptanceCriteria: .onOpenURL calls DeepLinkHandler.shared.handle(url) after the Supabase auth handle

MainTabView observes consumeDestination() and navigates, clearing after navigation
Tapping desmoinespulse.com/events/<id> opens the event detail in-app
Unmatched URLs fall back to the in-app browser without crashing

acceptanceCriteria: AppDelegate conforms to UNUserNotificationCenterDelegate and the delegate is set at launch

willPresent shows .banner,.sound for foreground notifications
Cold-launch from a notification lands on the right screen after init
Push notifications with a deep-link payload route correctly too

userStories.title: Index events and restaurants into Spotlight
userStories.description: As a user, I need the app's core content (events, restaurants) discoverable in system Spotlight so I can find it from outside the app.
acceptanceCriteria: EventsViewModel/RestaurantsViewModel call SpotlightService.indexEvents/indexRestaurants after fetch, capped to a reasonable count

userStories.title: Make Spotlight results deep-link into the app

acceptanceCriteria: CSSearchableItemActionType user activity handled; CSSearchableItemActivityIdentifier parsed (e.g. event-<id>)

Identifier parsing covers event/restaurant/article/hotel prefixes
Unknown identifiers fail gracefully to the home tab
userStories.notes:
VERIFIED DONE (2026-06-25): Full CSSearchableItemActionType path exists — DesMoinesInsiderApp.swift:114 onContinueUserActivity → DeepLinkHandler.handleSpotlightIdentifier (parses '<type>-<id>', routes event/restaurant/attraction) → MainTabView presents the detail. Covered by DeepLinkHandlerTests. No change needed.

userStories.title: Make the Ask Pulse quota-exceeded upsell reachable
userStories.description: As a free user who exhausts Ask Pulse, I need an upgrade CTA instead of a raw error so the monetization moment actually fires.
acceptanceCriteria: AskPulseService.ask detects the 429/quota response and throws .quotaExceeded
The view presents a paywall/upgrade CTA (PaywallView) instead of a raw error string
lastUsage.remaining is surfaced to the user before exhaustion
VIP/unlimited users never hit the quota path
userStories.notes:
DONE (2026-06-25): AskPulseService.ask now wraps functions.invoke('discover-chat') and maps a 429 (FunctionsError.httpError code 429, with a defensive body-text fallback) to AskPulseError.quotaExceeded, so the existing tailored upgrade CTA in AskPulseView fires instead of a generic error. Request payload + success Response shape untouched.

[prior] Evidence: AskPulseView.swift:274 catches .quotaExceeded but AskPulseService.ask (AskPulseService.swift:73-104) never throws it — a 429 falls into the generic catch with no upsell. | UX-audit root cause (2026-06-24): AskPulseError.quotaExceeded is never thrown — AskPulseService.ask only throws .notConfigured, so a 429 from discover-chat surfaces as a generic FunctionsError and the tailored upsell catch at AskPulseView.swift:274 is unreachable. Fix must inspect the HTTP status/body and throw .quotaExceeded for the upsell to fire.

userStories.title: Wire (or remove) the Trip Planner soft-paywall seam
userStories.description: As a free user, I need the engagement-based soft paywall to participate in the Trip Planner flow, or the dead seam removed, so the frequency-capped upsell isn't misleadingly half-built.
acceptanceCriteria: A free user's first Trip Planner Generate attempt triggers the capped soft paywall once (considerAfterTripPlannerAttempt called), respecting maxPresentations/cooldownDays
Analytics logs source: 'trip_planner'

userStories.title: Make the Surprise Me 'Save it' CTA actually save (or navigate)
userStories.description: As a user who taps the primary 'Save it — let's go' button on a Surprise Me pick, I need it to add the item to my favorites (or open its detail), because today it fires a success haptic, logs a 'saved' outcome, and dismisses without saving anything.

SurpriseMeView.swift:220 save(_:) calls notificationOccurred(.success) + track(outcome:.saved) + dismiss() with inline comment 'The actual favorite-add wiring lives in EventDetailView / RestaurantDetailView; for now, dismiss and let the user navigate.' The primary CTA adds nothing to favorites and offers no navigation — a dead-end. Confirmed by two independent audit passes. | DONE (2026-06-24): SurpriseMeView save now calls performSave() which favorites the pick via FavoritesService by item type (event/restaurant/attraction), guarding against toggling an already-saved item off; success haptic + track(.saved) + dismiss only on real save; limitReached dismisses for the app-level paywall; other errors show a 'Couldn't Save' alert + error haptic. get_surprise_pick returns only 'event'/'restaurant' (verified in migration).

userStories.title: Make Home 'For You' rail cards tappable to their detail screen

No regression to the rail's horizontal scroll/paging

userStories.title: Fix the consent screen that can never dismiss after the user chooses
userStories.description: As a first-launch user, I need the consent gate to advance after I Accept/Decline/Save, because ConsentService is @Observable but its consent values are UserDefaults-backed COMPUTED properties (not tracked), and the app presents ConsentView with an empty onComplete closure — so the gate's needsConsentPrompt branch is never re-evaluated and the screen can sit forever.
acceptanceCriteria: Choosing Accept / Decline / Save on ConsentView reliably advances past the consent gate on a fresh install

Root cause fixed: either back ConsentService's consent values with stored (observation-tracked) properties that mirror to UserDefaults, OR pass a real onComplete from DesMoinesInsiderApp that flips an @State flag the gate observes — the empty { } at DesMoinesInsiderApp.swift:47 must do real work
Re-launching the app does not re-show the consent gate once completed
Manual verification documented (fresh-install run, choose each path)
userStories.notes: Found by iOS UX audit. ConsentService.swift:14-17 exposes hasCompletedConsent/*Consent as computed UserDefaults getters/setters; @Observable only tracks stored properties, so writes don't notify SwiftUI. DesMoinesInsiderApp.swift:47 presents ConsentView { } with an empty onComplete, and dismissal depends solely on needsConsentPrompt flipping — which never re-fires. Potential hard launch blocker. | DONE (2026-06-24): Added locally-observed `consentCompleted` @State in DesMoinesInsiderApp; ConsentView presented with `{ consentCompleted = true }` and gate condition is now `consent.needsConsentPrompt && !consentCompleted`. Persisted hasCompletedConsent still suppresses the prompt next launch.

userStories.title: Give 'Restore Purchases' in Settings real success/failure feedback
userStories.description: As a user restoring a subscription from Settings, I need a spinner and a result message, because the button calls restorePurchases() but SettingsView never reads StoreKitService.isLoading/errorMessage — so nothing visibly happens whether it succeeds, finds nothing, or fails (an App Store review expectation for restore).
acceptanceCriteria: Tapping Restore Purchases shows an in-progress indicator while StoreKitService.isLoading is true
On completion it presents a clear result: 'Subscription restored', 'No purchases to restore', or the StoreKitService.errorMessage on failure
Pattern mirrors PaywallView.restore() (PaywallView.swift:599-611) which already does this correctly
Restore-failure (e.g. AppStore.sync() network error) is distinguished from a genuinely empty entitlement, not both shown as 'nothing to restore'
userStories.notes: Found by iOS UX audit. SettingsView.swift:42-48 Button { Task { await storeKit.restorePurchases() } } with no read of the service's isLoading/errorMessage. restorePurchases() (StoreKitService.swift:273) sets errorMessage and toggles isLoading but the view ignores both. Related: PaywallView.restore() masks AppStore.sync() failures as 'No active subscription found' (same fix for the distinguish-failure criterion). | DONE (2026-06-24): SettingsView restorePurchases() helper shows a ProgressView label + 'Restore Purchases' result alert; branches on storeKit.errorMessage (sync failure) vs currentTier != .free (restored) vs free (nothing found).

userStories.title: Stop the Favorites undo flow from dropping queued backend deletes
userStories.description: As a user removing several favorites quickly, I need each removal to actually persist, because starting a new undo cancels the previous removal's commitTask without ever committing it — the item is gone from the local array but viewModel.remove*Favorite is never called for it, so it silently resurrects on next load.
acceptanceCriteria: Removing a second favorite while a prior undo is still pending flushes (commits) the prior removal to the backend instead of just cancelling its task
After multiple quick removals with no undo taps, all removed items are gone from the server on reload (optimistic UI matches server truth)
Tapping Undo still restores exactly the most-recent removal
Implemented via a pending-removal queue or immediate commit-of-prior when a new removal starts (FavoritesView.swift:75/95/113)
userStories.notes: Found by iOS UX audit. FavoritesView.swift removeEventWithUndo/removeRestaurantWithUndo/removeAttractionWithUndo (lines 75, 95, 113) call undoState?.commitTask?.cancel() before replacing undoState, but never await the prior remove* call. Data-integrity bug: the optimistically-removed item is dropped from the array yet never deleted on the backend. | DONE (2026-06-24): Added flushPendingRemoval() in FavoritesView; the three remove*WithUndo paths now flush (commit) the prior pending removal to the backend before starting a new undo instead of cancelling its commitTask uncommitted.

userStories.title: Make the Ask Pulse pick card open the item detail (dead NavigationLink)
userStories.description: As a user, I need tapping the chevron on an Ask Pulse pick to open that event/restaurant/attraction, because the card is a NavigationLink(value: pick) with a 'Tap to open this … in detail' hint, but no .navigationDestination(for: Pick.self) exists anywhere, so the link routes nowhere.
acceptanceCriteria: Tapping an Ask Pulse pick card navigates to the matching detail screen, resolving pick.itemType+itemId to the real Event/Restaurant/Attraction (fetch by id as picks carry only id/type)
Add .navigationDestination(for: AskPulseService.Pick.self) on the AskPulseView NavigationStack, OR remove the chevron link and the 'tap to open' accessibility hint so there's no dead affordance
The accessibility hint matches the actual behavior
userStories.notes: Found by iOS UX audit. AskPulseView.swift:300 NavigationLink(value: pick) { chevron } inside the view's own NavigationStack (line 30); project-wide grep shows no navigationDestination(for: Pick.self). AskPulsePickCard advertises accessibilityHint 'Tap to open this … in detail' but nothing happens. | DONE (2026-06-24): Added .navigationDestination(for: AskPulseService.Pick.self) -> AskPulsePickDetailView, which resolves the pick by itemType to Event/Restaurant/Attraction via fetchEvent/fetchRestaurant/fetchAttraction(id:) with loading/failed/loaded phases. Chevron NavigationLink now reaches a real detail.

userStories.title: Apply (or remove) the Min Rating and Max Distance event filters

userStories.title: Make the VerifyEmailView refresh as promised, or fix its copy

userStories.title: Surface Trip Planner load failures and roll back failed optimistic writes
userStories.description: As a Trip Planner user, I need errors to show and the UI to match the server, because itinerary fetch failures render as a blank itinerary, and optimistic reorder/delete operations swallow backend errors so the on-screen state silently diverges and reverts on next load.
acceptanceCriteria: ItineraryDetailView distinguishes 'fetch failed' from 'genuinely empty': fetchItems signals failure (throw/optional) and the view shows an error+retry state instead of a blank body when online with no items (TripPlannerService.swift:106 currently returns [] on RPC error)
Reorder (move/persistOrder) reports success/failure; on failure it shows a toast and reloads to server truth rather than logging only in DEBUG (TripPlannerService.swift:156)

Trip delete awaits the backend result before mutating savedTrips (or re-inserts + shows an error on failure) so deleted trips don't reappear unexplained (TripPlannerView.swift:311, TripPlannerService.swift:143)
userStories.notes: Found by iOS UX audit. ItineraryDetailView.swift:187 sets loadFailed only when items.isEmpty && !network.isConnected; an online RPC failure yields a blank itinerary. move()/persistOrder and deleteTrips mutate local state optimistically and swallow errors (DEBUG-only logging), so the visible order/list can permanently disagree with the server. | DONE (2026-06-24): TripPlannerService.fetchItems now throws (caller distinguishes fetch-failure→loadFailed error+retry from genuinely empty); persistOrder returns Bool and deleteTrip returns Bool (@discardableResult). ItineraryDetailView.move reloads server truth + shows an error toast on persist failure (added toastOverlay + refetchItems). TripPlannerView.deleteTrips awaits each delete, and on any failure reloads server truth and sets errorMessage instead of silently dropping the trip.

userStories.title: Gate pull-to-refresh haptics on actual success across remaining screens
userStories.description: As a user, I need pull-to-refresh to signal success only when the refresh succeeded, because Hotels, Weekend, and Articles fire UINotificationFeedbackGenerator().notificationOccurred(.success) unconditionally even when the view model set an errorMessage — the exact false-success anti-pattern fixed elsewhere under IOS-AUDIT-UX-005.
acceptanceCriteria: HotelsView, WeekendView, and ArticlesView branch on viewModel.errorMessage == nil to play .success vs .error after refresh
DealsView's .refreshable closure gets success/error haptic feedback (currently none)
Behavior matches the already-fixed RestaurantsView/AttractionsView pattern
userStories.notes: Found by iOS UX audit. HotelsView.swift:76, WeekendView.swift:62, ArticlesView.swift:79 all call notificationOccurred(.success) unconditionally while their VMs set errorMessage on failure (HotelsViewModel:82, WeekendViewModel:52, ArticlesViewModel:106). DealsView.swift:64 has no refresh haptic at all. | DONE (2026-06-24): HotelsView/ArticlesView/WeekendView refresh haptics now branch on viewModel.errorMessage == nil ? .success : .error (canonical UX-005 pattern). DealsView .refreshable gained the same success/error haptic.

userStories.title: Show a stale-data error banner instead of a misleading empty state
userStories.description: As a user whose refresh fails while a filter is active, I need to see the real error, because Deals and Weekend hide a genuine load error behind a 'No Deals Found / clear filters' or featured-rails-only view when filtered/section data is empty but other data loaded.
acceptanceCriteria: DealsView surfaces the stale-data error banner when errorMessage != nil even if some allDeals exist but filteredDeals is empty, instead of showing 'No Deals Found' (DealsView.swift:25)

WeekendView decouples its error banner from isEmpty: an inline error+retry shows when errorMessage != nil and day sections are empty, even if featured rails populated (WeekendView.swift:29; isEmpty at WeekendViewModel.swift:25-27)
Genuine empty (no error) still shows the empty state; failures always offer retry
userStories.notes: Found by iOS UX audit. DealsView.swift:25 only shows the error when allDeals.isEmpty. WeekendView.swift:29 gates errorBanner on 'errorMessage != nil && isEmpty' where isEmpty also requires featured rails empty — so an events-fetch failure with featured rails present hides the error and shows zero events with no explanation. | DONE (2026-06-24): WeekendView shows errorBanner inline when errorMessage != nil && populatedDays.isEmpty (events failed but featured rails loaded). DealsView shows errorBanner instead of 'No Deals Found' when filteredDeals empty and errorMessage != nil. Both banners already include Retry.

userStories.title: Stop showing the password-reset success message inside a 'Sign In Error' alert
userStories.description: As a user requesting a password reset, I need a neutral success confirmation, because the success path routes its copy through setError(), which sets showError, fires an error haptic, and is rendered by an alert titled 'Sign In Error' — so a successful reset looks like a failure.
acceptanceCriteria: resetPassword() success uses a separate info/success channel (e.g. infoMessage) with a neutral alert title, not setError
No error haptic on the success path
Error cases still use the error alert + haptic
userStories.notes: Found by iOS UX audit. AuthViewModel.swift:204-205 success calls setError('Password reset email sent...'); setError (222-226) sets showError=true + notificationOccurred(.error); AuthView.swift:179 renders .alert('Sign In Error', isPresented: $viewModel.showError). | DONE (2026-06-24): AuthViewModel gained infoMessage/showInfo + setInfo() (success haptic); resetPassword success now calls setInfo. AuthView renders an 'Email Sent' info alert separate from 'Sign In Error'.

userStories.title: Animate the Discover action-bar Skip/Save/Boost like a swipe
userStories.description: As a user, I need tapping the Skip/Save/Boost buttons to fly the card off like a gesture swipe, because the handlers call viewModel.skip/like/boost directly and snap the top card away instantly, while gesture commits animate — and the intended bridge methods exist but are never called.

No visual snap/jump on button taps
userStories.notes: Found by iOS UX audit. DiscoverView.swift:219 button handlers call viewModel.skip/like/boost directly (instant removal); the animated programmatic* methods in SwipeCardStack are defined but grep confirms zero call sites. | DONE (2026-06-24): SwipeCardStack gained a @Binding command (enum Command: skip/like/boost) consumed via .onChange to drive the existing programmaticSkip/Like/Boost animated commit (guarded against re-entrancy). userStories.title: Prevent the 'all done' empty-state flash during a Discover boost
userStories.description: As a user swiping up to boost, I need the deck to stay coherent, because boost() sets deck = [] then refetches without setting isLoading, so the deckArea momentarily shows the 'You've seen everything / Reset deck' empty state before new cards arrive.
acceptanceCriteria: boost() sets isLoading = true before clearing/refetching and clears it when fetchMore completes (DiscoverViewModel.swift:235), OR keeps the previous deck visible until the new batch is ready

DiscoverViewModel.swift:235 boost() does deck = [] then Task { fetchMore() } with no isLoading; DiscoverView.swift:158-162 then falls through to the empty/all-done branch because 'isLoading && deck.isEmpty' is false. | DONE (2026-06-24): DiscoverViewModel.boost() sets isLoading=true before clearing the deck and clears it after fetchMore(), so the loading state shows instead of flashing the all-done empty state mid-boost.

userStories.title: Show a loading state during the search debounce instead of a blank screen

acceptanceCriteria: SavedSearchResultsView renders a loading state until the first search completes rather than a blank body (SavedSearchResultsView.swift:36)
SearchViewModel exposes an initial loading flag (e.g. hasLoadedOnce / isSearching defaulting true on first run) so the 300ms debounce window shows ProgressView (SearchViewModel.swift:50-53)
Genuinely-empty results still show the empty state after the search resolves

SavedSearchResultsView.swift:36 .task sets viewModel.searchText = savedSearch.query; performSearch sleeps 300ms before isSearching=true, so during the window isSearching=false & hasSearched=false → none of the states render. | DONE (2026-06-24): SearchViewModel.performSearch now sets isSearching=true synchronously before the 300ms debounce (and clearResults sets it false), so SavedSearchResultsView/SearchView show their ProgressView during the debounce window instead of a blank screen.

userStories.title: Fix the Trip Planner share-link failure shown under a 'Calendar' alert
