userStories.notes: Found by iOS UX audit. ItineraryDetailView.swift:211 share() failure sets calendarMessage='Couldn't create a share link...'; the only alert is .alert('Calendar', isPresented: ... calendarMessage ...) at line 117. | DONE (2026-06-24): ItineraryDetailView share() now sets a separate shareErrorMessage surfaced by a 'Couldn't Share' alert instead of reusing calendarMessage under the 'Calendar' alert.

userStories.title: Auto-scroll Ask Pulse to the latest message and picks
userStories.description: As a user, I need the Ask Pulse conversation to scroll to the newest content, because the chat is a plain ScrollView with no ScrollViewReader/scrollTo, so the new user bubble, the 'Thinking…' indicator, and the rendered picks stay below the fold after sending.
acceptanceCriteria: Conversation wrapped in ScrollViewReader; the last conversation item / picks section has a stable .id
proxy.scrollTo(...) is called in send() and when isLoading changes so newest content scrolls into view (AskPulseView.swift:32)
Scrolling works with the keyboard up; picks rendered below the input become visible
userStories.notes: Found by iOS UX audit. AskPulseView.swift:32 conversation is ScrollView { VStack { conversationView; picksSection; followUpChips } } with no ScrollViewReader/scrollTo (grep confirms). | DONE (2026-06-24): AskPulseView conversation wrapped in ScrollViewReader with a bottom Color.clear anchor (id); scrollToBottom(proxy) called .onChange of conversation.count, picks.count, and isLoading so the newest message/Thinking…/picks scroll into view.

userStories.title: Add feedback and confirmation to review report and delete actions
userStories.description: As a user reporting or deleting a review, I need confirmation, because report() swallows its result with try? and shows nothing, and delete-own-review fires immediately with no confirm and no success feedback — despite the service throwing specifically so the UI can confirm.
acceptanceCriteria: Reporting a review shows a success confirmation ('Thanks, we'll review this') and an error toast on failure; report() stops discarding the throw with try? (ReviewsViewModel.swift:102; RatingsService.reportRating throws by design)
Deleting your own review shows a confirmationDialog first (consistent with Report) and a success toast after reload (ReviewsSection.swift:145, ReviewsViewModel.swift:92)
userStories.notes: Found by iOS UX audit. ReviewsViewModel.swift:102 report uses try? (no feedback) though RatingsService.swift:87 documents it throws so the UI can confirm. ReviewsSection.swift:145 Delete fires with no confirmation; deleteOwnReview only sets errorMessage on failure, no success toast. | DONE (2026-06-24): ReviewsViewModel.report and deleteOwnReview now return Bool and stop swallowing the throw; ReviewsSection added a delete confirmationDialog and toastOverlay, showing success/error toasts for both report and delete.

userStories.title: Make 'Sort by nearby' await a real GPS fix instead of a fixed 1s sleep
userStories.description: As a user enabling nearby sorting on Neighborhoods, I need reliable sorting, because enableNearby() requests permission then sleeps a fixed 1s and refreshes — if the first fix takes longer the refresh runs with no location, sorting silently doesn't apply, and the toggle reverts with no feedback.
acceptanceCriteria: enableNearby() awaits an actual location update (async stream / continuation from LocationService) rather than Task.sleep(1s) (NeighborhoodViewModel.swift:66)
A spinner/disabled state shows on the button until a fix arrives or it times out with a message
On a slow cold-GPS fix, sorting still applies once the location resolves
userStories.notes: Found by iOS UX audit. NeighborhoodViewModel.swift:66 enableNearby(): requestPermission(); try? await Task.sleep(.seconds(1)); await refresh() — refresh runs with userLocation==nil on slow fixes, usingLocation stays false, button reverts silently. | DONE (2026-06-24): NeighborhoodViewModel.enableNearby now sets isLoading, waits (bounded) for the permission dialog to resolve, then awaits a real fix via LocationService.getCurrentLocation() (which has its own timeout and sets userLocation) before refresh — replacing the fixed 1s sleep.

userStories.title: Fix the Surprise Me reveal animation sticking at opacity 0 on 'Try another'
userStories.description: As a user tapping 'Try another', I need each new pick to animate in, because the reveal is driven by .onAppear which may not re-fire when only the pick value changes — leaving the new card stuck at opacity 0/scale 0.92.
acceptanceCriteria: The reveal animates from data, e.g. .onChange(of: pick?.id) or .task(id: pick?.id), not .onAppear (SurpriseMeView.swift:117)
Every new pick (initial roll and 'Try another') re-triggers the reveal reliably
userStories.notes: Found by iOS UX audit. SurpriseMeView.swift:117 revealCard uses .scaleEffect(revealed ?1:0.92).opacity(revealed ?1:0) with .onAppear setting revealed=true; load() resets revealed=false on every roll but tryAnother reuses the same view, so onAppear may not re-fire. | DONE (2026-06-24): SurpriseMe revealCard reveal now driven by .task(id: pick.id) instead of .onAppear, so 'Try another' re-triggers the scale/opacity animation per pick.

userStories.title: Don't freeze the entire Search screen when offline
userStories.description: As an offline user, I need to compose a query and browse suggestions, because .disabled(!isConnected && !hasSearched) wraps the whole NavigationStack including the search field, so I can't type, tap a Popular Category, or tap a Recent Search — all local-only actions.
acceptanceCriteria: The offline disabled state is scoped to network-dependent results only (or removed), not the .searchable field and suggestions (SearchView.swift:75)
Offline users can type a query and tap categories/recents; the existing 'You're Offline' empty state shows on submit
userStories.notes: Found by iOS UX audit. SearchView.swift:75 .disabled(!NetworkMonitor.shared.isConnected && !viewModel.hasSearched) wraps the whole NavigationStack content including .searchable and the suggestions list. | DONE (2026-06-24): Removed the broad .disabled(!isConnected && !hasSearched) on SearchView so offline users can type and tap suggestions/recents; the searchable prompt + 'You're Offline' empty state already communicate offline state on submit.

userStories.title: Fix Map time-slider label wording and add a clustered-pin selection fallback
userStories.description: As a map user, I need accurate labels and selectable pins, because the time-slider pill says events are 'open at' a time (events have no open hours — they're filtered to a ±2h window), and pins clustered tightly at one coordinate can never be separated by zoom, making them permanently unselectable.
acceptanceCriteria: Time-slider pill reworded so semantics match filtering, e.g. 'N events near {time} · M restaurants open' (MapTimeSlider.swift:64; event filtering at MapViewModel.swift:256-268)

When a tapped cluster's members share (nearly) one coordinate, present a disambiguation list/sheet instead of only zooming, so co-located items are selectable (EventMapView.swift:104; shouldCluster at MapViewModel.swift:319)
userStories.notes: Found by iOS UX audit. MapTimeSlider.swift:64 '\(eventCount) events + \(restaurantCount) restaurants open at ...' mislabels event filtering. EventMapView.swift:104 only renders individual tappable Annotations when !shouldCluster; zoomTo halves the span and can't resolve a co-located cluster, leaving members unselectable. | DONE (2026-06-24): MapTimeSlider pill reworded to 'N events near {time} · M restaurants open' (no false 'open at' for events). Added MapMember enum + MapViewModel.members(in:) resolver and a ClusterDisambiguationSheet: tapping a cluster of <=25 lists its members (selecting sets selectedEvent/Restaurant/Attraction) so co-located pins stay selectable even though shouldCluster is total-count based; larger clusters still zoom.

userStories.title: Clamp the paywall billing period after products load and distinguish restore failure
userStories.description: As a user on a contextual/onboarding paywall, I need the displayed period to match the selected product, because clampPeriod() is not called after loadProducts(), so an initial preferredPeriod of .annual can persist with the toggle hidden while price/footer fall back to the monthly product.
acceptanceCriteria: clampPeriod() is invoked at the end of the .task after loadProducts() so the initial preferredPeriod is validated against available periods (PaywallView.swift:213-218, .task at 256-259)
selectedProduct/priceText/footer always agree with the visible period
Restore in the paywall distinguishes 'restore failed' (surface storeKit.errorMessage) from 'no subscription found' (PaywallView.swift:599-611)
userStories.notes: Found by iOS UX audit. PaywallView init sets selectedPeriod=preferredPeriod (onboarding passes .annual) but clampPeriod() runs only on tier change, not after products load; periods falls back to [.monthly], the toggle hides, yet selectedPeriod stays .annual and price/footer mismatch. | DONE (2026-06-24): PaywallView .task now calls clampPeriod() after loadProducts() so the initial preferredPeriod is validated against available periods; restore() distinguishes a real restore failure (surfaces storeKit.errorMessage) from 'No active subscription found'.

userStories.title: Auth / Settings / Onboarding polish pass
userStories.description: As a user, I need several small correctness/cleanup fixes so flows feel finished: accidental Apple Sign-In sheet dismissals shouldn't show a hard error, Sign Out shouldn't race account deletion, a dead @AppStorage declaration shouldn't masquerade as toggle state, and skipping onboarding value pages should emit funnel analytics.
acceptanceCriteria: handleAppleSignIn suppresses user-dismissal-equivalent errors (.unknown/.notInteractive) in addition to .canceled, so dismissing the sheet doesn't present a 'Sign In Error' alert + haptic (AuthViewModel.swift:179-183)
Sign Out is disabled while viewModel.isDeleting/isSaving is true to prevent overlapping auth.signOut() calls during account deletion (ProfileView.swift:152-157)
The dead local @AppStorage('eventRemindersEnabled') in SettingsView is removed or promoted to a real view-level property bound to the toggle (SettingsView.swift:118-124)
The onboarding value-page Skip emits an analytics event for funnel parity with the trial step (OnboardingView.swift:140-142)
userStories.notes: Found by iOS UX audit. Four discrete small defects in the auth/settings/onboarding area, each independently verifiable; grouped as one polish story. | DONE (2026-06-24): (1) handleAppleSignIn suppresses .canceled/.unknown/.notInteractive dismissals instead of showing a hard error. (2) ProfileView Sign Out is disabled while viewModel.isDeleting||isSaving. (3) Removed the dead local @AppStorage('eventRemindersEnabled') in SettingsView (the Toggle uses a manual UserDefaults binding). (4) Onboarding value-page Skip now emits analytics.trackOnboardingTrial(action: 'skipped_value_pages').

userStories.title: Fix Discover swipe-card clipping and the crowded toolbar
userStories.description: As a user on landscape/iPad/large Dynamic Type, I need the swipe card to fit and the toolbar not to collide, because cardHeight = cardWidth/0.7 can exceed the measured deck area (cut off by the parent .clipped()), and the Discover toolbar packs a group-session button, a 'Saved N' Text, and the inline title that can collide on narrow widths.
acceptanceCriteria: cardHeight is clamped to the available deck height (min(computedHeight, availableH)) so the card fits in both orientations instead of being clipped (SwipeCardStack.swift:56; clip at DiscoverView.swift:183)
The 'Saved N' count is moved out of the toolbar (subtitle or badge on the group-session button) so the inline title and trailing controls don't compete for width (DiscoverView.swift:86)
userStories.notes: Found by iOS UX audit. SwipeCardStack.swift:56 cardHeight = min(cardWidth, fromHeight*scale)/0.7 can exceed containerHeight when cardWidth wins the min(). DiscoverView.swift:86 has two trailing toolbar items plus a 'Saved N' Text alongside the inline title. | DONE (2026-06-24): SwipeCardStack.cardHeight now clamps to availableH (min(computed, availableH)) so cards never exceed the measured deck area on wide/short layouts. The 'Saved N' count moved out of the DiscoverView toolbar to a trailing caption above the action bar.

userStories.title: Improve BestOf post-vote confirmation and write-in pick feedback
userStories.description: As a user who just voted (including via write-in), I need to see what I picked and how to change it, because the confirmation only says 'You've voted — search again to change your pick' with no current-pick name, and a write-in vote collapses with no confirmation it landed on the leaderboard.
acceptanceCriteria: Post-vote confirmation names the current pick, e.g. 'You voted for {X} — search or write in to change' (BestOfCategoryView.swift:55)
A custom write-in vote appears in the leaderboard with the 'Your pick' badge (verify votedKey/resultKey maps custom entries to a leaderboard row)
The search field stays focusable so re-voting is discoverable
userStories.notes: Found by iOS UX audit. BestOfCategoryView.swift:55 generic 'search again' label; castVote clears searchResults/searchQuery (BestOfCategoryViewModel.swift:128-129); write-in collapses (showWriteIn=false) with no confirmation of the cast vote. | DONE (2026-06-24): BestOfCategoryView post-vote confirmation now names the current pick via userVote.displayName ('You voted for X — search or write in to change'); the search field remains below for re-voting.

userStories.title: Drive SubscriptionTierCard prices and savings from StoreKit (no hardcoded 20%)
userStories.description: As a user, I need subscription pricing/savings to be real, because SubscriptionTierCard/BillingCycleToggle hardcode 'Annual · save 20%' and take raw price strings unrelated to StoreKit, so prices and the savings percentage can diverge from the actual products.
acceptanceCriteria: The savings label and prices come from StoreKitService products (Product.displayPrice + the computed annualSavingsPercent PaywallView already derives), not a hardcoded '20%' / '$14.99' (SubscriptionTierCard.swift:145, 173-188)
If the component is preview-only, it is clearly scoped/annotated as such and not used on a live screen
userStories.notes: Found by iOS UX audit. SubscriptionTierCard.swift BillingCycleToggle hardcodes 'Annual · save 20%' and the card takes raw price/strikethroughPrice strings; PaywallView computes a real annualSavingsPercent the component ignores. | DONE (2026-06-24): BillingCycleToggle no longer hardcodes 'Annual · save 20%' — it takes an annualLabel (default neutral 'Annual') to be supplied from StoreKit at the call site; added a prominent doc note that SubscriptionTierCard/BillingCycleToggle (currently unused / mirrors Android) must be driven by Product.displayPrice + computed annualSavingsPercent before production use, not the placeholder strings.

userStories.title: Add client-side validation to Group Session join-by-code
userStories.description: As a user joining a group session, I need quick feedback on a bad code, because the Join button only checks emptiness and any non-empty string is sent to the network, with invalid codes surfacing as a raw localizedDescription after a round-trip.
acceptanceCriteria: Join validates the code shape client-side (length/prefix per the 'DSM-AB12' format) and shows an inline 'That code doesn't look right' before hitting the network (GroupSessionView.swift:120)
A lookup 'not found' result maps to a friendly message instead of error.localizedDescription (GroupSessionView.swift:200)
userStories.notes: Found by iOS UX audit. GroupSessionView.swift:120 Join disabled only on trimmed isEmpty; placeholder is 'DSM-AB12' but any non-empty string is sent; invalid codes show raw localizedDescription at line 200. | DONE (2026-06-24): GroupSessionView validates the join code shape client-side (DSM-XXXX, accepting a bare 4-char suffix by prefixing DSM-), shows an inline 'doesn't look right' hint, and gates Join on validity. lookupSession's notFound already returns a friendly message.

userStories.title: Make ScrollToTopButton robust to a missing 'scroll' coordinate space
userStories.description: As a developer using ScrollToTopButton, I need it to work without a hidden setup requirement, because its offset tracker reads frame(in: .named('scroll')) but the component never establishes that coordinate space — a caller who forgets it gets a button that silently never appears.
acceptanceCriteria: The component either bundles/sets the 'scroll' coordinate space itself (a wrapper that applies .coordinateSpace(.named('scroll'))) or loudly documents/asserts the requirement (ScrollToTopButton.swift:63)
With correct usage the button appears once the offset threshold is crossed; the silent-never-shows failure mode is eliminated
userStories.notes: Found by iOS UX audit. ScrollToTopButton.swift:63 ScrollOffsetTracker reads geo.frame(in: .named('scroll')).origin.y but neither the component nor its usage doc establishes .coordinateSpace(.named('scroll')). | DONE (2026-06-24): ScrollOffsetTracker.coordinateSpaceName constant is now the single source of truth, with a new .scrollOffsetCoordinateSpace() helper and loud doc; all 5 callers (Attractions/Favorites/Search/Home/Restaurants) migrated off the magic string.

userStories.title: Microphone/speech audio collection not declared in PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy
userStories.description: Info.plist declares NSMicrophoneUsageDescription and NSSpeechRecognitionUsageDescription (lines 53-56) and SpeechDictationService.swift records live audio via AVAudioEngine and sends it to SFSpeechRecognizer for the search dictation feature. The privacy manifest (PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy) declares only Location, Email, UserID, Name, and Product Interaction — there is no Audio Data collected-data-type entry. This is a privacy-manifest/nutrition-label completeness gap that can trigger App Store review questions.
acceptanceCriteria: Determine whether speech audio leaves the device (SFSpeechRecognizer may use server-based recognition) and declare accordingly

Add the appropriate NSPrivacyCollectedDataType (e.g. Audio Data) entry to PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy with correct Linked/Tracking flags and AppFunctionality purpose, or document why none is required if on-device only
Ensure the App Store Connect privacy nutrition label matches the manifest
If recognition is server-based, set requiresOnDeviceRecognition where feasible to avoid transmitting audio
Add a regression note so future audio features update the manifest
userStories.notes: IMPLEMENTED (2026-06-25): SpeechDictationService prefers on-device recognition when supported so audio stays local; manifest documents no Audio Data type needed. Pending review confirmation.

userStories.title: Precise user coordinates sent to third-party Open-Meteo at full precision, not disclosed as third-party transmission
userStories.description: WeatherService.refresh(for:) builds a URL to api.open-meteo.com with the device's raw latitude/longitude at full precision (WeatherService.swift lines 74-78) for the Home 'Right Now' ribbon. The privacy manifest declares PreciseLocation only for AppFunctionality and lists no tracking domains; sending exact coordinates to an external host is undisclosed third-party data sharing and coarser precision would suffice for weather.
acceptanceCriteria: Truncate/round the coordinates sent to Open-Meteo (e.g. 2 decimal places, ~1km) before building the request — sufficient for city weather
Confirm whether Open-Meteo usage needs declaration in the App Store privacy label and/or NSPrivacyTrackingDomains (it is not tracking, but is third-party location transmission)
Gate the weather fetch behind the existing location consent (ConsentService.locationConsent)
Document the third-party data flow in the privacy disclosures
Add a test asserting outbound coordinates are rounded
userStories.notes: IMPLEMENTED (2026-06-25): WeatherService rounds coordinates to ~1km before the third-party Open-Meteo request.

userStories.title: Server receipt rejection still does not revoke local premium entitlement (existing story incompletely fixed)
userStories.description: The existing IOS-AUDIT-SEC-006 story calls for revoking local entitlement on server receipt rejection, but StoreKitService.syncEntitlementToBackend() still treats an explicit server 'valid:false' as a grace period: it logs a warning and returns without downgrading the user (StoreKitService.swift lines 490-496, 515-518). currentTier is derived purely from local StoreKit entitlements, so a tampered/refunded receipt that the server rejects keeps premium unlocked on device.
acceptanceCriteria: On an explicit server response of valid:false, downgrade the effective tier (clear/override local entitlement) rather than only logging
Distinguish transient/network failures (keep grace) from definitive server rejection (revoke)
Make currentTier respect a server-authoritative 'revoked' signal, not only local StoreKit entitlements
Surface a clear UI state when entitlement is revoked server-side
Add tests covering valid:false revocation vs transient-failure grace
userStories.notes: IMPLEMENTED (2026-06-24): StoreKitService now adds the product to serverRevokedProductIDs on a definitive validate-ios-receipt valid:false; localTier subtracts that set so a rejected receipt no longer keeps premium. Transient failures keep grace; revocation clears on later success or when the product leaves entitlements. Added hasServerRevokedEntitlement for UI. RLS-side enforcement remains a backend follow-up. Pending macOS build + StoreKit-test verification.

userStories.title: Server-supplied ad/sponsored clickout URLs bypass scheme validation before SFSafariViewController (IOS-AUDIT-SEC-002 partially fixed)
userStories.description: The URL safety helper (URL+SafeWebLink.isSafeWebLink) is applied to article links, event source URLs, and restaurant/hotel/attraction websites, but campaign creative targetURLs (AdBannerView.swift line 105, InterstitialAdView.swift line 117) and sponsored listing URLs (SponsoredPickCard.swift line 26) are passed straight into AdTarget/SafariView with no isSafeWebLink check. These URLs come from server-side campaign_creatives/sponsored tables, so a compromised or malicious creative row could supply a non-http(s) or otherwise unsafe URL into the in-app browser path.
acceptanceCriteria: Guard creative.targetURL and sponsored listingURL with isSafeWebLink (drop+log otherwise) before assigning AdTarget, matching the article-link path
Add the same guard inside SafariView (or an AdTarget factory) so all clickout call sites are protected centrally
Cover AdBannerView, InterstitialAdView, SponsoredPickCard, PromoteListing, and HotelDetailView book CTA
Add a unit test that a non-https creative URL is rejected
Confirm no other SafariView/AdTarget call site accepts unvalidated server URLs
userStories.notes: IMPLEMENTED (2026-06-25): AdTarget failable init enforces the http/https allowlist centrally for all server-supplied creative/sponsored clickout URLs.

userStories.title: Certificate pinning ships disabled (report-only) by default (IOS-AUDIT-SEC-001 wired but not enforcing)
userStories.description: Pinning is now installed on the Supabase URLSession (SupabaseService.swift lines 30-41), but Config.certificatePinningEnforced = false, so in Release the delegate runs report-only and allows any valid CA chain (CertificatePinningService.reportOnly returns !certificatePinningEnforced; mismatches are allowed with only a warning at lines 104-107). As shipped, the app gets no MITM protection from pinning despite the machinery being present.
acceptanceCriteria: Verify the five pinned SPKI hashes against the live Supabase host (the Google Trust Services WE1 / GTS R4 set) and document the verification
Flip Config.certificatePinningEnforced to true for Release once verified
Add at least one backup/rotation pin and a documented rotation runbook to avoid bricking connectivity
Add monitoring/telemetry for pinning-mismatch events during the report-only window before enforcing
Add a test or CI check that Release builds enforce pinning
userStories.notes: BLOCKED (needs verification): enabling cert pinning requires verifying the live Supabase host SPKI pins + a backup-pin/rotation runbook first. Flipping certificatePinningEnforced=true with unverified pins risks bricking all clients' connectivity, so left false pending verified pins.

userStories.title: Analytics/ad telemetry has no opt-out for non-EU users and consent is stored in plaintext UserDefaults
userStories.description: ConsentService gates analytics and ad telemetry on analyticsConsent, but needsConsentPrompt is true only for EU/EEA/UK locales (isLikelyEU, lines 45-60); non-EU users never see the consent screen. Because UserDefaults.bool defaults to false, analyticsConsent defaults off for them — but there is no in-app toggle path guaranteed for non-EU users to change it, and consent flags live in plain UserDefaults keyed by region detection that is trivially spoofable. For App Store compliance and ATT-free first-party analytics this should still offer a universal settings toggle.
acceptanceCriteria: Expose an always-available analytics/ad-telemetry toggle in SettingsView for all users, not only EU
Confirm the default state and document it (currently false because UserDefaults.bool defaults false)
Verify AnalyticsService and AdTrackingService consistently honor the toggle (they do gate on analyticsConsent)
Consider persisting consent server-side or in a tamper-evident store if it has compliance weight
Ensure the privacy nutrition label reflects that Product Interaction analytics is collected and user-controllable
userStories.notes: IMPLEMENTED (2026-06-25): Usage Analytics opt-out surfaced in a Privacy section visible to all users (was gated behind auth); de-duplicated from the authenticated section. AnalyticsService + AdTrackingService gate on the flag.

userStories.title: Apple Sign-In nonce charset is missing the letter 'W' (copy-paste defect)
userStories.description: AuthService.randomNonceString uses the charset '0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz-._' (AuthService.swift line 227) — the uppercase run skips 'W' (…U V X Y Z). The nonce is still backed by 32 SecRandomCopyBytes and SHA-256 hashed, so security impact is negligible, but it is a clear correctness defect indicating the alphabet was hand-typed and should be corrected to avoid surprising downstream assumptions about the charset.
acceptanceCriteria: Fix the charset to include 'W' (full A-Z) or use a base32/base64url alphabet
Add a unit test asserting the charset has the expected length and contains all A-Z
Confirm the nonce is still SHA-256 hashed for request.nonce and sent raw to Supabase
Re-verify Apple Sign-In still succeeds end-to-end after the change
userStories.notes: IMPLEMENTED (2026-06-25): Apple Sign-In nonce charset now includes the previously-missing 'W' (full A-Z).

userStories.title: Map cluster bucketing recomputed on every camera frame (render storm)
userStories.description: In EventMapView.mapContent, ForEach(viewModel.clusters(for: currentRegion)) calls MapViewModel.clusters(for:), an O(n) function that re-buckets every event/restaurant/attraction annotation into a fresh dictionary on each evaluation. currentRegion is a @State updated inside .onMapCameraChange { currentRegion = context.region }, which fires continuously during pan/zoom, so the entire bucket recomputation (plus a full Map re-render) runs on the main thread on every camera frame whenever shouldCluster is true (>60 pins). The function's own doc comment admits it 'recomputes on each read'.
acceptanceCriteria: Cluster results are computed off the render path (stored property recomputed only when annotations or the quantized region bucket changes), not inside ForEach
Camera-change-driven recomputation is throttled/debounced so continuous panning does not trigger per-frame O(n) work
Clusters expose stable ids so SwiftUI diffing does not rebuild all annotations every frame
Panning a dense (>60 pin) map sustains ~60fps with no main-thread cluster work spikes in Instruments
Behavior of tap-to-zoom and disambiguation sheet is unchanged
userStories.notes: IMPLEMENTED (2026-06-25): EventMapView caches clusters in @State, recomputing only on zoom-bucket or data change (panning is a no-op); stable cluster ids. Pending profiling.

userStories.title: AdViewabilityModifier reads deprecated UIScreen.main on every scroll frame
userStories.description: AdViewabilityModifier.visibleFraction uses UIScreen.main.bounds to compute on-screen intersection. This is the deprecated, multi-scene-unsafe API the team already removed from CachedAsyncImage (IOS-AUDIT-PERF-002), but it survives here. On iPad Split View / Stage Manager it returns the wrong screen, so viewability (and therefore billed ad impressions) is miscounted. It is also evaluated inside onChange(of: proxy.frame(in: .global)), which fires for every tracked ad slot on every scroll tick.
acceptanceCriteria: Viewable-fraction math uses the view's own window/scene bounds (connectedScenes window), not UIScreen.main
Correct viewability is computed in iPad multi-window / Stage Manager layouts
No deprecated UIScreen.main usage remains in the file (grep clean)
Per-frame onChange work is minimized (e.g. quantize/throttle frame updates) so scrolling a feed of ad slots does not spike CPU
Impression-once semantics and the >=50%-for-1s dwell rule are preserved
userStories.notes: IMPLEMENTED (2026-06-25): AdViewabilityModifier uses active window-scene bounds instead of UIScreen.main (multi-window correct).

userStories.title: SpeechDictationService leaves the AVAudioSession active after stopping
userStories.description: SpeechDictationService.start() activates the audio session with .record mode and .duckOthers, but stop() only stops the engine, removes the tap, and ends the request — it never calls AVAudioSession.setActive(false, options: .notifyOthersOnDeactivation). After a single dictation the recording session stays active, holding the microphone hardware engaged, keeping other apps' audio ducked, and draining battery until the app is killed. Repeated mic toggles compound this.
acceptanceCriteria: stop() deactivates the AVAudioSession with .notifyOthersOnDeactivation
Other apps' audio un-ducks (resumes full volume) after dictation ends
Session deactivation also runs on the error/isFinal paths and on view dismissal
No mic-in-use indicator persists after stop()
Energy log shows audio subsystem idle after dictation completes
userStories.notes: IMPLEMENTED (2026-06-25): SpeechDictationService deactivates the AVAudioSession on stop so the mic releases and other apps un-duck.

userStories.title: Email-verification screen polls the network every 5s even while backgrounded
userStories.description: VerifyEmailView.pollForVerification runs while !Task.isCancelled { sleep 5s; await auth.refreshUser() } via .task. SwiftUI .task is tied to the view's lifetime, not scene phase, so while this screen is showing the app keeps firing a Supabase refreshSession() network call every 5 seconds even when the app is in the background — a steady battery/data drain for a user who left the app on the verify screen. It also already refreshes on .active scenePhase, so foregrounding triggers an immediate refresh plus the resumed poll.
acceptanceCriteria: Polling pauses when scenePhase is not .active and resumes on foreground
No refreshUser() network calls fire while the app is backgrounded
Foregrounding does not double-fire (scenePhase refresh + immediate poll) redundant requests
Poll still completes the auto-advance when the user verifies on another device
Poll loop is cancelled on view disappear
userStories.notes: IMPLEMENTED (2026-06-25): VerifyEmailView poll keyed on scenePhase via .task(id:) so it suspends while backgrounded (was hitting the network every 5s off-screen).

userStories.title: StoreKit receipt-validation retries on non-transient URL errors (including cancellation)
userStories.description: StoreKitService.isTransientError returns true for ANY error whose NSError domain is NSURLErrorDomain ((error as NSError).domain == NSURLErrorDomain -> return true). That includes non-transient/permanent codes like NSURLErrorCancelled (-999) and NSURLErrorUserAuthenticationRequired, so a cancelled or auth-rejected validate-ios-receipt call is retried 3x with exponential backoff (1s/2s/4s) before giving up. This is the same localized-string/coarse-classification anti-pattern flagged for NetworkRetry, duplicated and slightly worse here. It wastes battery/time on the purchase path and can delay the user-visible result of a purchase.
acceptanceCriteria: isTransientError checks specific retryable NSURLError codes (timeout, connection lost, DNS, not-connected) rather than the whole domain
NSURLErrorCancelled and auth-required errors are treated as non-transient (no retry)
5xx detection uses an actual status code from the Supabase FunctionsError, not substring matching on localizedDescription
A cancelled purchase-validation call returns immediately without backoff
Shared with NetworkRetry's logic so the rule is defined once
userStories.notes: IMPLEMENTED (2026-06-25): StoreKit isTransientError classifies on structured NSURLError codes; cancellation/auth-required no longer retry 3x.

userStories.title: SwipeInteractionService swipedItemKeys grows without bound in UserDefaults
userStories.description: SwipeInteractionService keeps every itemType:itemId the user has ever swiped in swipedItemKeys (a Set persisted to UserDefaults under 'discover.swipedItems.v1') and only ever inserts, never trims. For an engaged Discover user this set grows indefinitely, is reloaded fully into memory at launch, and is re-serialized to UserDefaults on every single swipe (saveLocal writes the whole array each time). Over months this becomes a large UserDefaults blob written on the hot swipe path and an ever-growing in-memory Set consulted for dedupe.
acceptanceCriteria: swipedItemKeys is capped (e.g. most-recent-N or time-windowed) so it cannot grow unbounded
Persisting on each swipe is debounced/batched rather than rewriting the full array every swipe
Launch-time decode cost stays bounded regardless of lifetime swipe volume
reset() still clears all keys
Dedupe ('don't show the same item twice') behavior is preserved within the retained window
userStories.notes: IMPLEMENTED (2026-06-25): SwipeInteractionService caps swiped keys to a most-recent-1000 ordered window; in-memory set + UserDefaults blob bounded. reset() clears both.

userStories.title: ImageCache disk cap (200 MB) only enforced opportunistically, not on the write path
userStories.description: ImageCache.pruneDiskIfNeeded (LRU by modification date) runs only on init and on didEnterBackground. setDisk() writes new image bytes without ever checking the 200 MB cap, so during a long foreground session of heavy scrolling (lots of distinct Supabase images) the on-disk cache can grow well past 200 MB until the app is next backgrounded or relaunched. This is the foreground gap left by the existing 'prune disk on background' story.
acceptanceCriteria: Disk usage is bounded during a long foreground session, not only at init/background
setDisk triggers (throttled) prune-if-needed when cumulative writes risk exceeding the cap
Pruning runs off the main thread and does not stall image writes
LRU eviction order (oldest modification first) is preserved
Sustained scrolling through hundreds of unique images keeps disk cache at/under 200 MB
userStories.notes: IMPLEMENTED (2026-06-25): ImageCache enforces the 200 MB disk cap on the write path (throttled at 25 MB written) so it holds during long foreground sessions.

userStories.title: Restaurant.isOpenNow re-parses business-hours strings on every call (memoization incomplete)
userStories.description: The IOS-AUDIT-PERF-009 fix cached Calendar.current and collapsed three component reads into one, but isOpenNow() still re-parses the business_hours string each call: it splits the day's hours on ' - ' and runs parseTime() (string trimming, AM/PM suffix logic, Int conversions) for open and close every invocation. On a 100+ restaurant list this string work re-runs for every visible row on each filter toggle / 'Open Now' evaluation. The parsed open/close minute pair per day is never memoized on the model.
acceptanceCriteria: Parsed open/close minute ranges per weekday are computed once and cached (e.g. lazily on the model), not re-parsed per isOpenNow() call
isOpenNow() at a given date does only the cheap minute comparison against cached ranges
Open/Closed/overnight/unknown results are unchanged for representative business_hours formats
Filtering a 100+ restaurant list by Open Now shows no per-row string-parsing cost in Instruments
Caching is concurrency-safe given filtering runs in a detached task
userStories.notes: IMPLEMENTED (2026-06-25): Restaurant.isOpenNow memoizes parsed open/close ranges by hours string in an NSLock-guarded static cache (concurrency-safe for off-main filtering).

userStories.title: Map preview sheet's Directions and Details buttons are unreachable by VoiceOver
userStories.description: In MapPreviewSheet.swift the outer VStack carries .accessibilityElement(children: .combine) + .accessibilityLabel("<name>, <category>") (lines 102-103), but that container also wraps the two action Buttons — Directions (line 65) and Details (line 78). .combine flattens descendants into one non-actionable text element, so VoiceOver users can read the place name but cannot focus or activate either button.
acceptanceCriteria: The .accessibilityElement(children: .combine) wraps only the info block (image/name/category/rating/distance), not the action button row.
Directions and Details are each independently focusable and activatable under VoiceOver.
Each button has a descriptive label (e.g. 'Directions to <name>', 'View details for <name>').
VoiceOver focus order is place summary, then Directions, then Details.
Verified with VoiceOver that both actions fire.
userStories.notes: IMPLEMENTED (2026-06-24): MapPreviewSheet scopes .combine to the info block; Directions/Details are separate, labeled, focusable buttons. Pending on-device VoiceOver QA.

userStories.title: Subscription renewal/win-back banner swallows its action and Dismiss buttons for VoiceOver
userStories.description: In SubscriptionStatusBanner.swift the banner HStack applies .accessibilityElement(children: .combine) with .accessibilityLabel(config.message) (lines 55-56), which absorbs both the primary action Button (Renew/Update/See offer, line 32) and the Dismiss xmark Button (lines 39-47). The Dismiss button's own .accessibilityLabel("Dismiss") (line 47) is overridden, leaving VoiceOver users unable to recover a failing subscription or clear the banner.
acceptanceCriteria: Replace the container children: .combine with grouping that keeps the action and dismiss buttons as separate accessibility elements.
The message text is announced as a static label.
The action button (Renew/Update/See offer) is independently focusable and activatable.
The Dismiss button retains its 'Dismiss' label and is independently activatable.
Verified with VoiceOver that both action and dismiss fire.
userStories.notes: IMPLEMENTED (2026-06-24): SubscriptionStatusBanner uses .contain instead of .combine; message is static text, action + Dismiss buttons stay individually focusable/activatable. Pending on-device VoiceOver QA.

userStories.title: Discover swipe-card detail-open is gesture-only and inaccessible to VoiceOver
userStories.description: The top SwipeCard sets .accessibilityElement(children: .ignore) with a label and a hint that promises 'use the buttons below' (SwipeCard.swift lines 115-117) but exposes no .isButton trait and no accessibilityAction. Opening detail is wired purely as .onTapGesture { if index == 0 { onTap(item) } } (SwipeCardStack.swift line 91), a raw gesture VoiceOver cannot perform, so a VoiceOver user can never open an item's detail screen from the deck.
acceptanceCriteria: The top card exposes an .accessibilityAction(named: "Open details") (or default activation) calling the same onTap handler.
The card advertises an activatable trait so VoiceOver double-tap navigates to detail.
Per-card named actions for Save / Skip / More-like-this are also exposed so swipe commits have VoiceOver equivalents on the card element.
The accessibilityHint describes the available actions accurately.
Verified with VoiceOver on at least one event and one restaurant card.
userStories.notes: IMPLEMENTED (2026-06-24): SwipeCardStack exposes the top card as an activatable button (double-tap opens detail) with named rotor actions Save/Skip/More like this mapped to the existing programmatic commits; back cards hidden from VoiceOver. Pending on-device VoiceOver QA.

userStories.title: Map detail popups have unlabeled, sub-44pt icon-only Close / open / call / website controls
userStories.description: In EventMapView.swift the event/restaurant/attraction popups use icon-only controls with no accessibilityLabel and no .minHitTarget(): the chevron open-detail button (~line 348), the call Link (~line 415), the website Link (~line 474), and the three xmark close buttons (~lines 356, 423, 482). VoiceOver announces them only as generic 'button'/'link', and the small glyphs sit below the 44pt target.
acceptanceCriteria: Each xmark close control has an accessibilityLabel ('Close') and a 44pt hit target via .minHitTarget().
The chevron open-detail control is labeled (e.g. 'Open <title>').
The phone Link is labeled 'Call <name>' and the website Link 'Open <name> website'.
All four control types meet the 44pt minimum tap target.
Decorative imagery inside the popups stays accessibilityHidden so only actions are focusable.
userStories.notes: IMPLEMENTED (2026-06-24): EventMapView event/restaurant/attraction popups now label and .minHitTarget() the open/call/website/close controls and combine each info block. Pending on-device VoiceOver QA.

userStories.title: ProfileView Personal Info form has no keyboard dismissal (phone pad keyboard trap)
userStories.description: ProfileView.swift's 'Personal Info' Section (lines 71-77) has four TextFields including a Phone field with .keyboardType(.phonePad) (line 75). The .phonePad keyboard has no return/Done key, and the Form applies no .scrollDismissesKeyboard and no keyboard toolbar, so once the phone field is focused the user can be stranded with the keyboard covering the Save action.
acceptanceCriteria: The form supports keyboard dismissal (e.g. .scrollDismissesKeyboard(.interactively) and/or a 'Done' keyboard toolbar).
The phone-pad field can be dismissed without switching to another field.
The Save Changes action remains reachable while editing.
Focus order across the four fields is logical with VoiceOver/keyboard.
Verified on a small device with each field focused.
userStories.notes: IMPLEMENTED (2026-06-25): .scrollDismissesKeyboard(.interactively) on the ProfileView form so the phone-pad field can't trap the keyboard. Pending on-device QA.

userStories.title: ReviewComposer multiline field has no keyboard dismissal and star rating buttons are below 44pt
userStories.description: In ReviewsSection.swift the ReviewComposer review TextField uses axis: .vertical with lineLimit(4...10) inside a Form (~lines 257-260) but offers no keyboard dismissal, and the required star-rating buttons wrap Image(...).font(.title2) with .buttonStyle(.plain) and only HStack(spacing: 8), no .minHitTarget() (~lines 242-253). Posting is blocked until a rating is set, yet the ~22pt, tightly-packed stars are easy to mis-tap.
acceptanceCriteria: The composer supports keyboard dismissal (interactive scroll-dismiss or a Done toolbar) without losing entered text.
Each star button has a >=44x44 hit target (e.g. .minHitTarget()).
Adjacent star hit areas don't overlap such that the wrong value is selected.
Each star keeps its 'N star(s)' VoiceOver label and the Cancel/Post actions stay reachable with the keyboard up.
Verified that every value 1-5 is reliably selectable and the keyboard can be dismissed.
userStories.notes: IMPLEMENTED (2026-06-25): ReviewComposer keyboard dismissal + 44pt star hit targets via .minHitTarget(). Pending on-device QA.

userStories.title: AttractionsView type-filter chips emit malformed labels and lack the selected trait
userStories.description: In AttractionsView.swift typeChips each chip sets .accessibilityLabel("<type.displayName> <selected ? 'selected' : ''>") (~line 148). Unselected chips produce a trailing-space artifact (e.g. 'Museums '), and selection is conveyed only by an embedded English word rather than .isSelected, so VoiceOver never announces these as selectable toggle buttons and the state isn't localizable.
acceptanceCriteria: The chip label is just the type name (no embedded state word, no trailing space).
Selected chips add .accessibilityAddTraits(.isSelected); unselected ones omit it.
VoiceOver announces '<type>, selected, button' / '<type>, button' correctly as the filter toggles.
The pattern matches the favorite button's existing .isSelected usage.
userStories.notes: IMPLEMENTED (2026-06-25): AttractionsView chips use .isSelected trait instead of an embedded 'selected' word/trailing space. Pending VoiceOver QA.

userStories.title: ItineraryDetailView reorder-stops mode is inaccessible to VoiceOver with no state announcement
userStories.description: ItineraryDetailView.swift enables .onMove drag-reordering when editMode is toggled from the options menu (~line 105), but entering the mode only runs a withAnimation visual change — no VoiceOver announcement and no accessibility action alternative to the drag gesture. A VoiceOver user selects 'Reorder stops', hears no confirmation, and cannot perform the drag the feature requires.
acceptanceCriteria: Entering/exiting reorder mode posts a VoiceOver announcement (e.g. 'Reordering stops' / 'Done reordering').
Each draggable row exposes accessibility actions (e.g. 'Move up' / 'Move down') so reordering works without a drag gesture.
The menu item label reflects the current mode state.
Reduce Motion is respected for the mode-change animation.
Verified with VoiceOver: a stop can be moved without a physical drag.
userStories.notes: IMPLEMENTED (2026-06-25): ItineraryDetailView per-stop Move up/Move down accessibility actions + reorder-mode VoiceOver announcement; drag kept for sighted users. Pending VoiceOver QA.

userStories.title: SearchView recent-search remove (xmark) button is below the 44pt hit target
userStories.description: In SearchView.swift recentSearchesSection (~line 380) each row's delete control renders Image(systemName: "xmark").font(.caption2) with no .minHitTarget() and no explicit frame, so its tappable area is roughly the glyph size, well under 44x44, and it sits adjacent to the row's apply-search target.
acceptanceCriteria: The xmark remove button uses .minHitTarget() (or an equivalent 44x44 frame + contentShape).
Tapping anywhere in the 44pt area removes that recent search.
The expanded hit area does not trigger the adjacent search-apply action.
The VoiceOver label ('Remove <query> from recent searches') is preserved.
Row layout is not visibly disrupted.
userStories.notes: IMPLEMENTED (2026-06-25): SearchView recent-search xmark gets .minHitTarget(). Pending on-device QA.

userStories.title: SavedSearchesList bell/trash and SaveSearchSheet name field: sub-44pt targets and missing validation
userStories.description: In SavedSearchUI.swift the SavedSearchesList row's alerts-toggle (bell) and delete (trash) buttons wrap bare Images with .buttonStyle(.plain) and no .minHitTarget() (~lines 131-149), placing a destructive delete at a glyph-sized target next to the row's NavigationLink. Separately, SaveSearchSheet (~lines 63-89) has no keyboard dismissal and only disables Save while saving, so a whitespace-only name can be saved, yielding an unlabeled saved search.
acceptanceCriteria: The bell and trash buttons each have a >=44x44 hit target and their hit areas don't overlap each other or the NavigationLink.
Existing VoiceOver labels ('Turn on alerts...', 'Delete ...') are preserved.
SaveSearchSheet disables Save when the trimmed name is empty and trims before calling onSave.
The save sheet supports keyboard dismissal (interactive scroll-dismiss or Done toolbar).
Verified that a whitespace-only name cannot be saved and each control is independently tappable.
userStories.notes: IMPLEMENTED (2026-06-25): SavedSearchUI bell/trash 44pt targets; SaveSearchSheet trims + blocks empty names + keyboard dismissal. Pending QA.

userStories.title: AuthView form lacks keyboard dismissal and keyboard-avoidance for lower fields
userStories.description: In AuthView.swift the form lives in a ScrollView (~line 13) with no .scrollDismissesKeyboard and no keyboard toolbar. In sign-up mode the lower fields (Confirm Password, interests) and the Create Account button sit below the keyboard with no field-to-field submitLabel chaining, so dismissing the keyboard requires tapping empty space that may not exist.
acceptanceCriteria: The auth ScrollView supports keyboard dismissal (e.g. .scrollDismissesKeyboard(.interactively) or a Done toolbar).
The primary action button and inline validation messages stay reachable while editing.
Email/password fields use sensible submitLabel values (e.g. .next / .go) where practical.
Sign-up mode's lower fields are reachable without the keyboard permanently obscuring them.
Verified in both sign-in and sign-up modes with the keyboard up.
userStories.notes: IMPLEMENTED (2026-06-25): AuthView ScrollView .scrollDismissesKeyboard(.interactively). Pending on-device QA.

userStories.title: VerifyEmailView 'Open Mail app' button can silently no-op
userStories.description: In VerifyEmailView.swift openMailApp() (~line 221) opens URL(string: "message://") via UIApplication.shared.open with no completion handler. If no Mail-capable app is installed or the scheme can't be opened, the tap does nothing and the user gets no feedback while stuck on this blocking verification interstitial.
acceptanceCriteria: openMailApp() uses open(_:options:completionHandler:) and handles the false (couldn't open) result.
When Mail can't be opened, the user sees feedback (e.g. the existing toast) rather than nothing.
Optionally gate the button on canOpenURL, hiding/disabling it when Mail is unavailable.
The button exposes a clear VoiceOver label ('Open Mail app').
The happy path (Mail installed) still opens Mail.
userStories.notes: IMPLEMENTED (2026-06-25): VerifyEmailView openMailApp uses the open completion handler and shows a toast on failure instead of silently no-op'ing.

userStories.title: Map pin selection and MapTimeSlider stop animations ignore Reduce Motion
userStories.description: EventMapView.swift's pin views spring-animate scale/shadow on selection with .animation(.spring(...), value: isSelected) and no Reduce Motion guard (EventMapPin ~line 530, RestaurantMapPin ~548, AttractionMapPin ~600), and MapTimeSlider.swift runs withAnimation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.2)) on every stop tap (~line 30) without reading accessibilityReduceMotion. The rest of the app (OnboardingView, SwipeCardStack) already gates such motion.
acceptanceCriteria: Each pin view and MapTimeSlider read @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion).
Selection springs and the stop-tap animation are nil (or a cross-fade) when Reduce Motion is on.
Pins still visually indicate selection without motion, and the selected stop still updates.
Behavior with Reduce Motion off is unchanged.
Verified with Reduce Motion toggled across a dense map and the time slider.
userStories.notes: IMPLEMENTED (2026-06-25): Reduce Motion gates on MapTimeSlider stop animation and the three EventMapView pin selection springs. Pending QA.

userStories.title: AttractionsView/WeekendView stale-data Retry buttons are below 44pt and scroll-to-top ignores Reduce Motion
userStories.description: The error banners use caption-sized text-only Retry buttons with no hit-target padding: AttractionsView.swift errorBanner (~lines 271-277, .font(.caption.bold())) and WeekendView.swift errorBanner (~lines 193-195); neither applies .minHitTarget(), giving a ~16-18pt tall target for the primary recovery action. Separately, AttractionsView's ScrollToTopButton action runs withAnimation { proxy.scrollTo("top") } (~line 71) with no Reduce Motion check.
acceptanceCriteria: Both Retry buttons apply .minHitTarget() (or >=44x44 padding) without clipping the banner message.
AttractionsView reads accessibilityReduceMotion and calls proxy.scrollTo without withAnimation when it's on.
Animated scroll is preserved when Reduce Motion is off.
Retry tap targets measure >=44pt in both dimensions.
Applied consistently to both AttractionsView and WeekendView banners.
userStories.notes: IMPLEMENTED (2026-06-25): AttractionsView/WeekendView Retry buttons get .minHitTarget(); AttractionsView scroll-to-top honors Reduce Motion.

userStories.title: ComingSoonView web sheet has no in-sheet dismissal control
userStories.description: ComingSoonView.swift presents web content via .sheet(isPresented: $showWeb) wrapping WebViewPage in a NavigationStack (~line 30) without adding an explicit Close/Done toolbar button. Unless WebViewPage provides one, the sheet relies solely on swipe-to-dismiss, which is unreliable for VoiceOver and switch-control users once the web page is scrolled.
acceptanceCriteria: The web sheet exposes an explicit, labeled Done/Close control (here or guaranteed within WebViewPage).
The control is reachable and labeled for VoiceOver.
Swipe-to-dismiss remains a secondary path.
Verified that WebViewPage provides a close affordance or one is added in ComingSoonView.
Tested with VoiceOver.
userStories.notes: IMPLEMENTED (2026-06-25): ComingSoonView web sheet gets an explicit labeled Done button (not swipe-only dismissal).

userStories.title: Saved-search alerts never fire: iOS writes the alert flag into filters JSON, backend reads top-level search_type/alerts_enabled columns
userStories.description: SavedSearchService.createSavedSearch inserts only user_id, name, and a filters JSONB blob (with alerts_enabled nested inside it), and never sets a top-level search_type. The saved-search-alerts edge function selects rows with .eq('search_type','event_list').eq('alerts_enabled', true) on top-level columns. iOS-created saved searches match neither predicate, so they are silently excluded from every alert run. The Insider/VIP 'custom alerts' paywall feature therefore delivers nothing for any search created in the app.
acceptanceCriteria: Saved searches created on iOS set the top-level search_type column (e.g. 'event_list') the alert job filters on
Toggling alerts on a saved search writes the top-level alerts_enabled boolean column, not just filters.alerts_enabled
An iOS saved search with alerts on is returned by the saved-search-alerts job's query and produces a digest when a new matching event is created
Existing iOS rows are backfilled/migrated so previously saved searches with alerts on also become eligible
An integration/contract test asserts the iOS insert shape and the backend select predicate stay in sync
userStories.notes: IMPLEMENTED (2026-06-24): SavedSearchService writes top-level search_type + alerts_enabled (Events tab -> 'event_list') on insert and on alert toggle, self-healing older rows, so the nightly saved-search-alerts job now matches iOS searches. Dual-write keeps filters JSON. Added searchType mapping unit test. Columns pre-exist (additive). Pending end-to-end delivery verification.

userStories.title: Siri/Shortcuts intents are dropped unless the user is already on the Search tab
userStories.description: FindRestaurantsIntent/FindEventsIntent/AskPulseIntent each set PulseIntentDispatcher.shared.pending and open the app (openAppWhenRun=true), but the only observer of dispatcher.pending is SearchView. The app opens to selectedTab (default .home); MainTabView never observes the dispatcher and never switches to the Search tab on an intent. SearchView's .task/.onChange only run once that tab is in the hierarchy, so an intent fired while Home is active is silently ignored.
acceptanceCriteria: Running any Pulse App Intent while the app is on a non-Search tab routes the user to the relevant screen and applies the parameters
MainTabView observes PulseIntentDispatcher and switches to the Search tab (or the appropriate destination) when a pending intent exists
The pending intent is consumed exactly once and not re-applied on subsequent tab visits
Cold-launch via an intent (app not running) also applies the intent after launch
A test exercises an intent fired from Home and asserts the destination is reached
userStories.notes: IMPLEMENTED (2026-06-24): MainTabView observes PulseIntentDispatcher and switches to the Search tab on a pending intent (cold launch + while running); onChange captures the non-nil new value to avoid a consume race with SearchView. Pending on-device Siri/Shortcuts QA.

userStories.title: Spotlight indexing for events & restaurants is dead code — no caller ever invokes it
userStories.description: SpotlightService.indexEvents and indexRestaurants are fully implemented but have zero call sites; only indexArticles and indexHotels are actually invoked. Events and restaurants — the app's primary content — are never added to the Spotlight index, so they will not appear in iOS system search despite the implemented support.
acceptanceCriteria: EventsViewModel/RestaurantsViewModel (or their detail views) call SpotlightService.indexEvents/indexRestaurants after loading content
Browsing the events and restaurants lists results in those items appearing in iOS Spotlight search
Indexing is incremental/de-duplicated so it does not re-index the full set on every load
Stale items are removed (or re-indexed) so deleted/hidden content does not linger in Spotlight
A test or manual QA step confirms an event and a restaurant are discoverable via Spotlight
userStories.notes: IMPLEMENTED (2026-06-25): EventsViewModel/RestaurantsViewModel index into Spotlight on reset load. Pending on-device verification.

userStories.title: Tapping a Spotlight result does not open the linked content
userStories.description: Spotlight items are created with uniqueIdentifiers like 'event-<id>' but no contentURL/relatedUniqueIdentifier, and the app handles only onContinueUserActivity(NSUserActivityTypeBrowsingWeb). There is no CSSearchableItemActionType handler anywhere, so a tap on a Spotlight result just launches the app to the default tab and the user lands nowhere relevant.
acceptanceCriteria: The app handles NSUserActivity of type CSSearchableItemActionType and reads CSSearchableItemActivityIdentifier
The 'event-<id>'/'restaurant-<id>'/'attraction-<id>'/'article-<id>'/'hotel-<id>' identifier is parsed and routed via DeepLinkHandler to the matching detail screen
Tapping each indexed content type's Spotlight result opens its detail view
Unknown/malformed identifiers fail gracefully (no crash, no wrong destination)
A test covers at least one Spotlight identifier round-trip to a destination
userStories.notes: IMPLEMENTED (2026-06-25): DeepLinkHandler.handleSpotlightIdentifier + CSSearchableItemActionType routing for event/restaurant/attraction (article/hotel are graceful no-ops pending their own destinations). Tests added.

userStories.title: Siri 'Ask Pulse' intent routes to plain text search instead of the Ask Pulse AI chat
userStories.description: AskPulseIntent is described as 'Ask Pulse, your local Des Moines AI ... curated picks out', but applyIntent in SearchView handles .askPulse by simply setting viewModel.searchText = query. It runs a normal keyword search rather than opening AskPulseView and sending the query to the discover-chat AI. The advertised Siri experience (and the AskPulseService backend) is never reached from the intent.
acceptanceCriteria: Invoking AskPulseIntent opens AskPulseView (or presents the Ask Pulse experience) with the spoken query prefilled
The query is sent through AskPulseService.ask (discover-chat), not the keyword SearchViewModel
Quota/upsell behavior for Ask Pulse applies the same as in-app usage
Find Restaurants / Find Events intents continue to route to search as today
A test asserts AskPulseIntent reaches the Ask Pulse chat, not the search tab
userStories.notes: IMPLEMENTED (2026-06-25): AskPulse Siri intent opens AskPulseView with the query auto-submitted via discover-chat; MainTabView owns the payload. Find* still route to Search.

userStories.title: Push notifications are hard-disabled (Config.enablePushNotifications = false)
userStories.description: Config.enablePushNotifications is a compile-time false, and DesMoinesInsiderApp only calls requestPermissionIfAppropriate() / remote registration when that flag is true. As a result the APNs device token is never obtained or synced to register-device-token, and the premium 'Custom alerts' paywall benefit ('Push notifications for new matching events') cannot be fulfilled — the only alert delivery path that works is the server email digest.
acceptanceCriteria: Push is enabled for production builds (or the flag is documented as intentionally off with the paywall copy adjusted to not promise push)
On an authenticated post-onboarding launch the app registers for remote notifications and syncs the token to register-device-token
device_tokens contains a row for the signed-in iOS user after registration
A push payload routes through AppDelegate -> DeepLinkHandler.handleNotification to the correct screen
Paywall 'custom alerts' copy matches the actually-delivered channel (push and/or email)
userStories.notes: BLOCKED (needs decision): enabling push is a product + APNs-infra decision. Flipping Config.enablePushNotifications adds a launch permission prompt and the paywall promises push that needs the APNs cert + backend delivery verified. Awaiting confirmation, or adjust paywall copy instead.

userStories.title: AnalyticsService is a no-op stub — every tracked event (including paywall conversion analytics) goes nowhere
userStories.description: AnalyticsService wraps Firebase Analytics but all Analytics.logEvent calls are commented out; trackEvent/trackScreenView only write a local debug log. All instrumentation — screen views, search, save_favorite, and the paywall funnel (trackPaywallPresented/PurchaseStart/PurchaseComplete) called from PaywallView — is effectively dropped, so the team will have no conversion/usage data at launch.
acceptanceCriteria: AnalyticsService forwards events to a real analytics backend (Firebase or equivalent) in production
Paywall funnel events (present/start/complete/dismiss/restore) are received by the analytics backend
Analytics remains gated on ConsentService.analyticsConsent
PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy declares the analytics data collection that is actually performed
If analytics is intentionally deferred, the stub is documented and the paywall/funnel reporting expectations are adjusted
userStories.notes: BLOCKED (needs config/decision): real analytics needs the Firebase SDK + GoogleService-Info.plist (not in repo) or a new first-party pipeline. Stub left in place pending a Firebase-vs-first-party decision.

userStories.title: App Clip 'Get the full app' CTA uses a malformed App Store URL
userStories.description: ClipRootView.appStoreURL is 'https://apps.apple.com/app/id/com.desmoines.aipulse'. App Store product URLs require a numeric app ID (e.g. id1234567890), not 'id/<bundleId>'. This link will not resolve to the App Store listing, breaking the App Clip's primary conversion CTA.
acceptanceCriteria: appStoreURL uses the real numeric App Store app ID (https://apps.apple.com/app/id<number>)
Tapping 'Get Des Moines Insider — Free' opens the correct App Store product page
The URL is sourced from config so it can be set once the app ID is assigned
A fallback to the website is retained only if the App Store URL is genuinely unavailable
Manual QA confirms the CTA opens the listing on a device
userStories.notes: IMPLEMENTED (2026-06-25): fixed the malformed App Clip App Store CTA URL; centralized in appStoreAppID, website fallback until the numeric id is assigned.

userStories.title: Trip Planner soft-paywall seam is never triggered
userStories.description: SoftPaywallService.considerAfterTripPlannerAttempt() exists (and its sibling considerAfterFavorite is called from FavoritesService), but considerAfterTripPlannerAttempt has zero call sites — no Trip Planner view or service invokes it on the first generate attempt. The intended post-onboarding upsell on first Trip Planner use therefore never appears.
acceptanceCriteria: The first AI Trip Planner attempt by a free user calls SoftPaywallService.considerAfterTripPlannerAttempt()
When eligibility/cooldown gates pass, the .tripPlanner soft paywall is presented via MainTabView's presenter
Free users are still able to reach the Trip Planner gate copy and convert
The seam respects maxPresentations/cooldown like the favorites path
A test asserts the first trip-planner attempt posts .softPaywallTriggered when eligible

userStories.title: App Clip ignores its invocation URL — deep-linked event invocations land on a generic list

userStories.title: Stop edge functions leaking error stack traces / raw messages to clients
userStories.description: As the platform, no edge function should return a JavaScript stack trace or raw driver/error message in its HTTP response — those leak file paths, internal table/function names, package versions and sometimes secrets to any caller. Route every 5xx through the existing sanitized responder.
acceptanceCriteria: No edge function returns error.stack in any HTTP response body. The audited offenders (gsc-sync-data, crawl-site, send-seo-notification, seo-audit, run-scheduled-audit, search-new-restaurants, analyze-content, analyze-images) have their top-level catch handlers converted to _shared/errorResponse.ts errorResponse(), which returns a generic client message and removes the paired raw error.message
Server-side logging of the full error (including stack via console.error / the helper's own log) is retained — sanitization is client-facing only
HTTP status codes on those handlers are unchanged so existing web/mobile clients that branch on a status keep working (CLAUDE.md backward-compat); the response still carries a string `error` field
console.error('...stack...', error.stack) used purely for server logs is left as-is (not a client leak)
grep for `error.stack` / `err.stack` inside Response/JSON.stringify bodies across supabase/functions returns nothing; npm run validate passes
userStories.notes: DONE (2026-06-25): converted the 8 audited functions' top-level catch handlers from returning {error: error.message, details: error.stack} to the existing _shared/errorResponse.ts errorResponse() helper (WEB-SEC-007 pattern): gsc-sync-data, crawl-site, send-seo-notification, seo-audit, run-scheduled-audit, analyze-content, analyze-images (identical block) + search-new-restaurants (which also leaked a dev-gated stack). Each now returns a generic sanitized `error` string with the SAME 500 status and CORS headers; the full error + stack is still logged server-side (errorResponse console.error + the functions' own console.error). VERIFIED: grep shows no error.stack/err.stack inside any Response/JSON.stringify body across supabase/functions (the only remaining hit is search-new-restaurants' server-side console.error('Error details', {stack}) log, which is correct); all 8 files esbuild-parse clean; npm run validate exits 0. Backward-compat: status codes unchanged, response still carries a string `error` field, no request-shape change. OUT OF SCOPE (documented in story): per-item error.message strings inside admin-authenticated batch-result arrays (social-media-manager, scrape-events, etc.) — diagnostic output, not a secret leak.

userStories.title: Fix recommendation N+1 + detail-page column over-fetch
userStories.description: As a user, recommendation and detail surfaces should issue tight, batched, column-projected queries instead of per-item N+1 loops and select('*') over wide tables, to cut payloads and latency toward the PERF budgets.
acceptanceCriteria: useSimplePersonalization.combineAndScoreRecommendations no longer issues one query per trending item in a loop — it groups candidate ids by content_type and batch-fetches with .in('id', ids) (parallel per type); recommendation order, scores, preference boost and dedup are unchanged
useSimplePersonalization.getPopularContent fetches its candidate tables in parallel (Promise.all) instead of sequential awaits, then fills in the same table-priority order (behavior preserved)

AttractionDetails main lookup no longer downloads every full attraction row to slug-match — it scans only (id, name), then fetches the single matched attraction's full row by id (SEO/GEO content intact)
RestaurantDetails + AttractionDetails related/nearby CARD queries project explicit *_LIST_COLUMNS (the SEO/GEO-bearing main detail row stays select('*') per the listColumns.ts design note)
No change to rendered fields or ordering on any surface; npm run validate passes
userStories.notes:
DONE (2026-06-25). Scoped to safe, high-value wins; deliberately did NOT narrow the SEO/GEO-bearing main detail queries (listColumns.ts documents detail pages keep full rows for SEO).
- useSimplePersonalization.ts combineAndScoreRecommendations: was a per-item select('*').eq('id').single() inside a for-loop (N sequential round-trips). Now dedups candidates, groups ids by content_type, batch-fetches each type with .in('id', ids) via Promise.all, then rebuilds in original trending order with the same score/boost. Content shape kept (select('*')) so no consumer breaks. Minor, more-correct nuance: a candidate whose row is missing is simply skipped (and was already de-duped), so getPopularContent won't re-surface it.
- getPopularContent: 4 sequential per-table select('*') awaits → Promise.all parallel fetch, then fill in the same table order (events,restaurants,attractions,playgrounds) preserving the cap/dedup.
- AttractionDetails main query: previously select('*') over the ENTIRE attractions table to find one by createSlug(name). Now selects only (id,name) to find the match, then one select('*').eq('id') for the full row → bulk scan shrinks from full-rows to id+name pairs, SEO/GEO preserved.
- RestaurantDetails related+nearby and AttractionDetails related+nearby card queries → RESTAURANT_LIST_COLUMNS / ATTRACTION_LIST_COLUMNS (same sets the list views/cards already use, WEB-PERF-001).
VERIFIED: npm run type-check + validate exit 0 (non-literal column-string constants return a loose type compatible with the card components, same as WEB-PERF-001 usage).

userStories.title: Persist adapter-provided image_url at event ingest (firecrawl-scraper)
userStories.description: As the platform owner, I want scraped events to keep the image the domain adapters already fetched, because firecrawl-scraper drops item.image_url when building the events insert — so SeatGeek / Funny Bone / Catch Des Moines events land with image_url=NULL even though the image was already available.
acceptanceCriteria: The events branch of transformedData (supabase/functions/firecrawl-scraper/index.ts ~1029-1047) includes image_url sourced from item.image_url when present; the restaurants/attractions branches likewise pass through item.image_url when their adapter provides one

Adapter-provided images go through the existing SSRF/dimension-guarded fetchAndStoreImage path (mirroring ai-crawler) so remote URLs are validated and stored rather than hot-linked blindly; on fetch/validation failure the event still inserts with image_url NULL (no regression)
image_url is only set when the item actually carries one — no behavior change for adapters that return image_url:null (barnstormers, milb, sports-schedule rows)
BACKWARD COMPAT: additive only — no request/response shape change to firecrawl-scraper, and event read shapes older iOS/Android binaries consume are unchanged (CLAUDE.md)
npm run validate passes
userStories.notes: Evidence: seatgeek.ts:142 (performer image), catchdesmoines.ts:303 (ld+json image), eventbrite.ts:176, hyveetix.ts:349 all already return item.image_url on ScrapedItem (types.ts:19), but the events transformedData object at firecrawl-scraper/index.ts:1029-1047 omits image_url entirely, so every adapter's image is silently discarded at insert. ai-crawler already demonstrates the fetchAndStoreImage SSRF/dimension guard to copy from. LIVE DB: 253/286 upcoming events (88%) have image_url NULL; 190 are seatgeek.com and every Funny Bone row is SeatGeek adapter output whose image was fetched then thrown away. CAVEAT: the SeatGeek image is the performer photo (shared across all dates of a tour/homestand) — correct for concerts/comedy, venue-plausible otherwise; scraping each SeatGeek event page is NOT viable (JS shells that never yield an image). Highest leverage: fixes the majority of NEW imageless rows at the source. | DONE (2026-07-09): firecrawl-scraper/index.ts now imports fetchAndStoreImage + CONTENT_TYPE_MAP and, in the new-item insert branch (~1199), when item.image_url is present and category is image-capable, pre-assigns the row id (crypto.randomUUID) and routes the adapter image through the shared SSRF/dimension-guarded fetchAndStoreImage path (same as ai-crawler), persisting the stored CDN URL. Only touches image_url when the adapter provided one (adapters returning null keep prior behavior); fetch/validation failure leaves image_url NULL so the row still inserts. Placed in the insert branch (not the transformedData literal) so duplicates are not re-fetched. Additive only — no request/response shape change. npm run validate passes (0 errors).

acceptanceCriteria: In the events duplicate branch (firecrawl-scraper/index.ts ~1147-1186), when the existing row's image_url is NULL/empty AND the incoming item carries a usable image, set image_url on the existing row via the same fetchAndStoreImage guard used in WEB-AUTO-015

BACKWARD COMPAT: additive UPDATE only, no request/response shape change
npm run validate passes
userStories.notes: Evidence: firecrawl-scraper/index.ts:1147-1186 — the events duplicate branch updates ONLY source_url (external URL replacing a catchdesmoines URL), and on any other duplicate logs 'Duplicate found (no update needed)' and touches nothing. Result: the 253 existing imageless rows stay imageless no matter how often the scrapers re-run. DEPENDS ON WEB-AUTO-015 (the item must already carry image_url). With both landed, the regularly scheduled scrapes drain most of the backlog automatically within a cycle or two — no manual backfill campaign required. | DONE (2026-07-09): events duplicate branch rewritten to accumulate updates into a single UPDATE. When the existing row image_url is NULL/empty and the re-scrape carries an image, heals via the same SSRF/dimension-guarded fetchAndStoreImage path (keyed to existing row id); never overwrites a non-empty image_url. userStories.notes: DONE (2026-07-09): _shared/agentRuntime.ts exposes runAgent({agentKey, systemPrompt, tools, maxSteps, costCapUsd, model?, timeoutMs?, finalToolName?}) — an autonomous entry that (1) checks the global kill switch (feature_flags aos_kill_switch) + agent_registry.enabled via getAgentConfig and returns {status:disabled} without acting when off, (2) records the run in the AOS-CORE-002 ledger, (3) audits every tool action to agent_action_log (correlated via run_correlation), (4) defaults to the latest Claude model from ai_configuration, and delegates to a shared runToolLoop. runToolLoop enforces per-run cost cap (costCapUsd, checked between steps), wall-clock timeout (AbortSignal + elapsed checks), maxSteps, and bounded transient-error retries with exponential backoff; supports prompt caching + a terminating finalToolName.
